feature: Remediation Tracking: the findings-derived checklist (#3038, Feature #1489) -- the 'Your findings' and 'Fixed outside change control' tabs of the real customer-facing '/remediation-tracking' page in artifacts/portal, wiring §1b-1e of docs/portal/remediation-tracking-contract-pack.md: GET/PUT /api/portal/remediation/checklist(/:checkKey), POST .../checklist/:checkKey/raise-change, GET /api/portal/remediation/fix-routes, POST /api/portal/remediation/fix-routes/:checkKey/reveal, and GET /api/portal/remediation/bypass-resolutions. No fixture module: every row on screen comes from these endpoints. The page's third tab, the 28-step programme (§1a/§1f/§1g), is #3037/#3039's scope -- see test-manifests/portal/remediation-tracking.json for that coverage; this file is this build's own findings-derived slice of the same page.
notes: WHAT THIS COVERS: the three real GET reads (checklist/fix-routes/bypass-resolutions) answering 200 with the shapes the page's hooks consume, and the accepted_risk write guard on the checklist's own PUT — a bare `status: "accepted_risk"` is rejected 400 (#2827/#2869; the route's real, signed exit is POST .../decline-to-risk, not covered by this manifest since it creates a permanent msp_risk_decisions row). A real writable status (not_started) round-trips 200 against a stable monitor_checks key so the write path is proven without leaving persistent tracker state behind on re-run.

SEEDED DATA: uses a real, stable monitor_checks.key (identity:mfa-method-breakdown) rather than a scan-derived finding, since the checklist's item LIST depends on the test tenant's latest scan having open critical/warning findings, which is not guaranteed to be stable across runs — the write tests below exercise the same remediation_tracker_steps table the checklist GET reads, keyed by checkKey, independent of whether that check currently has an open finding.

ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD — the same CustomerUser testbed account test-manifests/portal/notification-preferences.json already uses. All three GET routes and the PUT route require only requireRole("Assessment"), the lowest role carrying a customerId claim.

shaneapp://runTest WAS ACTUALLY INVOKED (2026-09-06, session for #3038), not skipped by assumption — same real, repeatable envelope `{ ok:false, error:'manifest not found or unparseable: remediation-tracking-checklist.json' }` the sibling #3037 build's own manifest documents for the identical structural reason: BuildConsole's dev-server checkout has not yet merged/restarted onto a commit carrying this file. Not a runTest defect. Verified instead by a real `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` pass (0 errors) and a real `vite build` (succeeds) against artifacts/portal with this page section/hooks/components added, plus direct reading of every route file this manifest exercises (portal-remediation-checklist.ts, -fix-routes.ts, -bypass-resolutions.ts) confirming every status/shape asserted below. Re-run via shaneapp://runTest once the dev-server merge/restart cycle has caught up.

#3346 (2026-09-09): the checklist card's own 'Decline and accept the risk' affordance (ChecklistItemCard.tsx's DeclineToRiskDialog) is now wired to the same POST .../decline-to-risk route A4's guard proves the write-side of, matching the current Design export and the real precedent already shipped for the 28-step programme's StepActionDialog decline mode. No new API surface: the button/dialog call the existing useDeclineChecklistItemToRisk hook against the same endpoint. WHY NO CLICK-THROUGH UI STEP IS ADDED FOR IT: same reason remediation-tracking.json's own '§1a decline-to-risk happy path' note gives — the route creates a PERMANENT signed msp_risk_decisions row and 409s on a repeat attempt against the same check, and this manifest's checklist item LIST (per the SEEDED DATA note above) depends on the test tenant's latest scan having an open critical/warning finding, which is not guaranteed stable across runs; there is no stable checkKey guaranteed to appear as a live checklist row to click against. Verified instead by the same tsc/build pass this file already documents, plus direct reading of ChecklistItemCard.tsx confirming the button is gated on `item.status !== "accepted_risk" && item.verificationState !== "verified"` (mirroring the Design export's own canDecline predicate) and that an already-accepted item renders the read-only 'Signed acceptance' badge instead (mirroring StepRow.tsx's identical real precedent for the programme tab).

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated testbed portal account; extract the bearer.
A1 -- the findings-derived checklist (§1b) answers 200 with an items array, honest-empty for an untouched/clean tenant rather than a fixture.
A2 -- the fix-route dimension (§1c) answers 200 with a real tenantWriteCeiling and an items array.
A3 -- the bypass-resolutions correlation (§1e) answers 200 with an items array, purely observational.

A6 -- a real writable status round-trips 200 against a stable check key, proving the write path without leaving non-default state behind on re-run (not_started is the table's own absence default).
